summary: @servicetitan/confirm-navigation ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (_0xNNNNNN identifier scheme, dictionary-lookup call wrappers) and, on npm install, downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmod+x's the bun binary, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line bundle with obfuscator.io fingerprints (shuffled string/numeric array n7gIxM, rotation function WV8StW, decoder hc1jfK9). The executed bytes are the shipped obfuscated bundle — Bun is only the loader, chosen to evade Node-based inspection tooling. A react-router navigation-confirmation UI helper has no legitimate need to fetch a JS runtime at install time or to execute an obfuscated multi-hundred-KB payload. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with homepage docs.st.dev, so the malicious release is either a scope compromise or lookalike targeting developers who trust the ServiceTitan brand.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
